DECISION: flatMerge NOT adopted — the bead's premise dissolved under the D14 rewrite. The push-sync loop it targeted no longer exists (createTable.ts has no sync loop; the options store is a pull-based writable memo whose compute re-layers the STABLE getter-carrying mergedOptions object). The two remaining flatMerge candidates both lose: (1) the mergeOptions binding (setOptions path) — flatMerge EVALUATES getters, so the first setOptions would freeze table.options.data to a snapshot: a correctness regression, not a granularity tradeoff; (2) the store compute — eager evaluation makes the store track every caller signal, so any option change invalidates every table.options reader (the coarsening the bead warned about). EVIDENCE per acceptance: new tests/unit/optionsGranularity.test.ts pins per-key invalidation on the live adapter (data-signal change fires only the data reader effect, enableSorting reader stays quiet, and vice versa) — the granularity flatMerge cannot preserve by construction; the lazy chain's read-cost side is already benchmarked in mergeObjects.test.ts (200-layer case, from 65n.1). Chain depth on the hot path is a small construction-time constant; it only grows via repeated imperative setOptions (cold path). flatMerge stays vendored+tested if a future shape needs it. Gates: test:lib 148/148, tsc 0, eslint green. Commit follows.
